newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi ports handle 87 million tonnes in 1994.
newsitem.headline: Saudi ports handle 87 million tonnes in 1994.

text.p: Saudi ports handled 87 million tonnes of goods, excluding crude oil, in 1994, up five percent on the previous year, the Saudi Seaports Authority (SSA) said in its latest annual report.

Exports in the year totalled 57.1 million tonnes, Saudi newspapers on Sunday reported the SSA report as saying. It said major exports in 1994 were refined petroleum products, petrochemicals, liquid natural gas, sulphur and wheat.

Imports of commercial goods stood at 25.6 million tonnes in the year, while industrial good imports were around four million tonnes. Food, building materials, motor vehicles and machinery were the main imports.
In the year, the kingdom imported over 4.5 million head of livestock, of which 19 percent came from New Zealand, it said.

King Fahd Industrial Port in Jubail was the busiest port in 1994, handling 28 million tonnes, followed by King Fahd Port in Yanbu, which handled 27 million tonnes of petroleum products and petrochemicals.

Of the harbours handling commercial goods, Jeddah Islamic Port was the busiest, with 19 million tonnes passing through it in 1994, followed by King Abdul-Aziz Port in Dammam, with nine million tonnes.
